transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. I, um... well, I work as a veterinary technologist, and the clinic has been so busy lately. We had this poor Golden Retriever in yesterday with a twisted stomach, and the owners were just crying and crying in the waiting room. It's so hard seeing people like that, you know? I always try to comfort them, because animals really are just family. My own dog passed away a few years ago and I still haven't really gotten over it, to be honest. I actually still have his collar hanging on my rearview mirror in my car. 

Which... I guess that's sort of why I'm here. Because lately, when I'm looking at that mirror, driving home from the clinic... I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. It just scared me enough to finally make an appointment, because I keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up at all.
Are you wanting to kill yourself?

I... I don't know if "want" is the right word. It's more like... well, like I was just saying about the drive home. I drive a Subaru Outback, and they're supposed to be incredibly safe cars. My brother-in-law sold it to me, actually—he manages a dealership over in Springfield and he's always talking about their crash safety ratings. He's a real car guy, you know, can talk for hours about crumple zones and airbags. 

But... yeah, that's what scared me enough to come in. Despite how safe the car is, I just catch myself on that drive, right at the big curve by the reservoir, wondering what would happen if I just didn't turn the wheel. If I just let it go straight. And then at night... I just keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. Like, if I could just skip the waking up part entirely. I used to really love mornings, too. I have this beautiful copper French press for my coffee that I got at an artisan market a few years back, but I don't even use it anymore. It just sits on the counter getting dusty...
Have you ever decided that you would act on these thoughts?

Decided? No, I... I haven't actually made a plan or, you know, marked a date on a calendar or anything. I still use a physical paper calendar, actually. It's one of those ones with different dog breeds for every month that my niece gets me for Christmas every year. She's in college now, studying marine biology down in Florida. I always tell her she should try to work with manatees, they're just such gentle creatures, you know? And the water down there is so warm compared to here. The winters here just drag on forever and the roads get so awful and icy... 

Which, I guess... um, what was I saying? Oh, right, deciding to do it. No, I haven't decided to actually do anything. But like I was saying a minute ago, what really scared me into finally coming in today is just how heavy it all feels, and how I just keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up at all. I haven't made a choice to end things, but when I'm on that drive home... I just keep catching myself wondering what would happen if I didn't turn the wheel. I haven't decided to do it, but the fact that my brain keeps going there is just really frightening to me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah, I... I have. It's like... most days I just feel like the color has completely drained out of everything. Which is strange to say, because my house is actually painted these really bright, vibrant colors. My husband and I painted the living room this beautiful sunflower yellow when we first moved in. He used to work at a hardware store, so he got all the paint at a discount. They had this whole mixing machine and he'd come home with paint chips in his pockets... 

But even with the bright walls, and even when the house is busy with him and the kids—well, they're teenagers now, so they're always in and out with their friends, tracking mud everywhere—even with all that life around me, I just feel this heavy, gray hopelessness. It gets so bad that I end up hiding in the laundry room just to cry. I sit on the floor next to the dryer because it's warm, and I just weep. I don't want any of them to see me like that, you know? I don't want them to see how absolutely hopeless I feel. The laundry room is the only place I can really be alone, since our cat doesn't like the noise of the spin cycle. She's a calico, a rescue from the clinic, actually... but yeah, I just feel so down.
Did these feelings start after a particular loss or stressful event?

No, not really. I mean, nothing specific happened right before it started. It's just been hanging over me for... gosh, about 11 months now? Though this past month has just made everything feel completely unbearable. But yeah, 11 months. Which is funny, because 11 is my lucky number. I always buy two lottery tickets when the jackpot gets high, and I always make sure one of the numbers is 11. My uncle won $500 on a scratch-off once, and he bought this huge, ridiculous riding lawnmower. Our yard isn't even big enough for a riding mower, but he just loved driving it around in circles. He used to let the neighbor's kids sit on his lap while he mowed... 

But anyway, no, there wasn't a death or a big fight or anything like that. Just... almost a whole year of this heavy cloud. And then this last month, it just got so much worse.
Before this past 11 months, have you ever had another period like this where you felt depressed most days for at least two weeks?

Before this past 11 months? Um... no, not that I can remember. I don't think I've ever had a stretch like this before. I mean, everyone has bad days, especially at the clinic. We had this one awful week right before all this started where our digital x-ray machine completely broke down. It was a total nightmare. The repair guy, Dave—he's this sweet older man who always brings a box of glazed donuts when he comes—he had to order a replacement part all the way from Germany. Germany! Can you imagine the shipping costs on a specialized medical part from Europe? My husband and I actually went to Europe for our honeymoon years ago. We took this incredible train ride through the Alps, and the scenery was just breathtaking. And the cheese there... oh my goodness, we went to this tiny little dairy farm and I swear I could have eaten my weight in it. The cows all had those big bells around their necks, just like you see in the movies... 

But, wait, what was I... oh, right, feeling depressed before. No, honestly, I really don't think so. It's just been this one long, terrible stretch.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?

Worrying? No... no, I wouldn't say I worry about a bunch of different things. I just feel so weighed down by the sadness, I don't really have the energy to worry. I don't have that nervous, pacing kind of feeling. 

Not like some of the animals we see at the clinic, anyway. We have this one regular, a Weimaraner named Duke, and he has the most terrible nervous energy. He literally chewed through a solid wooden door frame once when a thunderstorm rolled in. Wood! Can you imagine the splinters? We had to carefully check his whole mouth and throat. It reminded me of when my son was little and he got a massive splinter in his foot from the boardwalk at the beach. We were on vacation in Ocean City, and they have those great big buckets of caramel popcorn there. Oh, I used to love that popcorn. The seagulls there are so aggressive, though, one actually swooped down and snatched a piece right out of my hand while we were walking near the pier... 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, right, worrying. No. I don't really have that. Just the heavy feeling.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, completely. I used to love photography and gardening, and bird watching... but I haven't touched my camera in months. I don't even check the bird feeders anymore. I don't care what's coming up in the garden. It's actually really frightening because those things used to be how I felt like myself, you know? 

My camera is this beautiful old Nikon. My husband bought it for our 20th anniversary. We went out to this fancy Italian restaurant to celebrate, the one downtown with the valet parking? The valet was so young, he couldn't have been more than sixteen, and he looked terrified to drive my husband's truck. It's a big Ford F-150, bright red. My husband loves that truck more than anything, except maybe his fantasy football team. He spends hours every Sunday just staring at his phone, checking the scores. I never really understood football. All those guys just crashing into each other... it seems so violent. Like those big rams you see on nature documentaries, just bashing their heads together over and over. I saw a documentary once about animals in the Rocky Mountains, and the scenery was just... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just... I don't have any interest in the things I used to love. It's all just gone.

Trouble sleeping? Yes, it's been awful. I just lie awake at night, staring at the ceiling, replaying everything I’ve ever done wrong in my life. Like this one time at the clinic, I accidentally sent the wrong prescription diet home with Mrs. Gable. She has this massive orange tabby cat named Barnaby—he honestly looks like a furry pumpkin with legs. We were supposed to give him the metabolic weight-loss kibble, but I handed her the renal support bags instead. Feline kidney issues are so tricky, you know? They hide it so well until they're really sick. My uncle actually had terrible kidney stones a few years back. He said the pain was worse than breaking his leg. He ended up in the emergency room right in the middle of Thanksgiving dinner! We had to eat the turkey without him, and my aunt tried to carve it but the knife was completely dull. She basically shredded the poor bird. We ended up buying her one of those electric carving knives for Christmas that year... they make this awful buzzing sound, kind of like a hornet's nest? I've always been terrified of hornets ever since I got stung at a summer picnic when I was little... 

But... I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my sleep. Yeah, so if I'm not lying awake agonizing over things, I'm waking up way before dawn, just completely exhausted. And even when I force myself to stay in bed longer, I just never feel rested enough to go for my runs or even just function normally during the day. I'm just always so tired.
